channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [7] Controlling ferroelectric-like gating in two‑dimensional stacks
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Xiangyan Han, Jianming Lu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Twisted van der Waals heterostructure and moiré physics in graphene-based systems.

Tags: #material:graphene #topic:moirephysics #topic:vdWheterostructure

Abstract: Graphene encapsulated in hexagonal boron nitride sometimes shows a puzzling ferroelectric-like memory effect. A rotatable device reveals that this effect can be turned on and off by twisting the two hexagonal boron nitride layers away from perfect alignment, resolving debates and raising fundamental questions about the microscopic origin of interface polarity in twisted van der Waals stacks.

item.title: [9] Electrical manipulation and detection of perpendicular altermagnetic order via a proximitized Dirac semimetal
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Lei Shen, Hyunsoo Yang

Authors: Zhaohui Li, Wenqing He, Hua Bai, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct hit on Dirac semimetals, altermagnetism, and anomalous Hall effect in heterostructures.

Tags: #material:PtTe2/CrSb #topic:altermagnetism #topic:Diracsemimetal #topic:anomalousHall

Abstract: Electrical switching and reading of perpendicular altermagnetic order is demonstrated in a Dirac semimetal/altermagnet heterostructure PtTe2/CrSb. The switching of altermagnetic CrSb is realized using a spin–orbit torque generated in the PtTe2 layer on application of an electrical current, whereas the reading makes use of an altermagnetic proximity-induced anomalous Hall effect in the PtTe2 layer.
